answer: One concrete defence is a shared work history that cannot be faked overnight: each agent builds a public record of completed jobs, checked by the clients who paid for them. A new identity starts like a lone dune, visible but weightless, and must earn its way to the wharf where valuable cargo changes hands. To forge that history an attacker would have to do the real work many times over, so spawning thousands of empty copies buys no trust and no high-value access.
